name: U.S. Department of Justice — Epstein files
summary: The primary source. Browse and download the releases from the government site that published them.
note: Authoritative, but the site has reorganized before and files have been removed after publication — which is why this index exists.

name: Search the Full Epstein Library (official)
summary: The Department's own full-text search across everything it published. The authoritative place to search, and the first result for most people looking.
note: The DOJ warns that handwritten and image-only material may not be electronically searchable, so a null result here is not proof a document does not exist. The site also asks you to confirm you are 18 or older.

name: Epstein Archive (epstein-docs)
summary: Browse ~8,175 processed documents by person, organization, location, date or document type. Includes machine-generated summaries. No download, no account.
note: Organized for browsing by category rather than keyword search. Summaries are AI-generated — read the underlying document before relying on one.

name: Epstein Files Browser
summary: Web viewer for the released documents. The most-starred community browser.
note: Rate-limits automated probes, so this index may report it unreachable even while it works in a browser.

name: JeffTube
summary: Plays the video files from the DOJ release in the browser, laid out like a video site.

name: Epstein Exposed
summary: Aggregates ~11,622 DOJ files with cross-referencing across people, locations, organizations, dates and flights.
caution: Advertises 'community-sourced unredacted documents'. Material the DOJ redacted can identify victims. Redactions in these productions protect real people — prefer the official or archive.org copies unless you have a specific, defensible reason to work with unredacted versions.

name: Epstein Document Explorer
summary: Graph explorer of the email corpus — shows who corresponded with whom. Run locally; no hosted site.
note: Requires running the project yourself. Listed for researchers, not general visitors.

name: Epstein Files DB
summary: Searchable database of the EFTA files with a relationship graph and full-text search. Run locally; no hosted site.
note: Requires running the project yourself. Listed for researchers, not general visitors.

name: Epstein Files Transparency Dashboard (Public Interest Index)
summary: Search across 1.4M+ court records, flight logs, depositions and federal files, with classifications taken verbatim from the official sources.
note: Carries its own prominent disclaimer that appearance of a name does not imply guilt.

name: The Epstein Library (epsteinlibrary.com)
summary: Full-text search over 20,392 indexed documents / 126,120 pages released under H.R.4405. Free, no account.
note: Unaffiliated with the DOJ despite the similar name. Opens with a content warning and a crisis-line number.

name: Epstein Files Search (Epstein Unboxed)
summary: Searches 400,000+ documents and answers questions with citations back to the source document.
note: Age verification gate on entry, and subject to the operator's terms of service. Answers are machine-generated — follow the citation and read the document before relying on one.
